title: The Civil Service and Public Corporations

blocks.text: Ministers come and go with each President. The files in the Federal Secretariat do not. A permanent secretary who served a PDP minister in 2014 may brief an APC minister in 2015 on the same water project. That continuity — and the rule that the official's name must not appear on the policy — is the civil service.

blocks.title: Civil service
blocks.text: The body of permanent, professional officials employed by the state to advise the political executive and to implement government policy. In Nigeria it exists at federal and state levels, headed administratively by permanent secretaries and overseen politically by ministers or commissioners.

blocks.markdown:
### Features and functions

The civil service is **hierarchical**: authority runs from the Head of the Civil Service and permanent secretaries down through directors to clerks. It is **impersonal** — decisions are supposed to follow rules, not family or party. Recruitment and promotion are in principle by **merit**, through the Federal or State Civil Service Commission. Officials are expected to be **impartial** between citizens.

Its functions are to **advise** ministers on policy options, **implement** decisions and statutes, **draft** bills, regulations and briefs, **keep records**, **collect revenue** and manage expenditure under the Appropriation Act, and provide **continuity** when the political executive changes.

rows: Officials keep their posts when the government changes; they do not resign with a defeated party
So the state does not have to rebuild its administration after every election
Civil servants do not take public credit or public blame for policy; they are not named as the authors of decisions
So the minister, who is accountable to the National Assembly and the electorate, remains the public face
Officials serve whichever party is in power, without using their office to favour that party or sabotage its successor
So the same machinery can implement a new government's programme the morning after an election
Each officer is responsible to a superior, up to the permanent secretary and the minister
So instructions are clear and responsibility can be located
Officials are recruited and trained for specialised work — finance, health, works, foreign affairs
So ministers, who are politicians, have professional advice
blocks.caption: Classic features of the civil service. Anonymity, neutrality and permanence are the three that examinations ask for by name

blocks.markdown:
### Ministers and permanent secretaries

A **minister** is a political executive: appointed by the President, confirmed by the Senate, and dismissed at the President's pleasure. He or she makes policy, defends it in public and in the National Assembly, and is the person the public blames or praises.

A **permanent secretary** is the administrative head of the ministry: a career official who controls the files, coordinates departments, advises the minister and sees that approved policy is carried out. When the minister is moved, the permanent secretary stays — that is permanence in practice. The relationship fails when a minister bypasses the permanent secretary, or when a permanent secretary withholds information from an unwelcome minister.

items: **Public corporations** are statutory bodies created by law to provide commercial or utility services that the state wishes to control — electricity, telecommunications, railways, steel, airways.

**Historical Nigerian examples**: the National Electric Power Authority (**NEPA**), later the Power Holding Company of Nigeria (**PHCN**); Nigerian Telecommunications Limited (**NITEL**); the Nigerian Railway Corporation; Nigeria Airways; the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation in its earlier fully state-owned form.
**Reasons for creating them**: to provide essential services regardless of profit; to control strategic industries; to raise revenue; to pursue development where private capital would not go.

**Problems**: inefficiency and overstaffing; political interference in appointments and pricing; corruption; poor maintenance; dependence on government subvention; inability to meet demand (blackouts under NEPA/PHCN; decaying NITEL lines).

**Privatisation and commercialisation**: from the Structural Adjustment Programme of 1986 and the Privatisation and Commercialisation Decree of 1988, through the Bureau of Public Enterprises. NITEL was sold (with a troubled history of buyers); PHCN was unbundled into successor generation and distribution companies. The aim was efficiency and reduced fiscal burden; the political cost has been job losses and public suspicion of asset sales.

blocks.title: Civil service is not a public corporation
blocks.text: A ministry is funded from the budget and does not sell a product; a public corporation is set up by statute to run a service that could, in principle, charge users. NEPA was a corporation; the Federal Ministry of Power was not. Mixing the two is a frequent examination error.

blocks.title: Applying anonymity, neutrality and permanence
blocks.prompt: A new minister of health, from a party that has just defeated the incumbent, finds the same permanent secretary still in post. The minister wants the official to appear on television defending a new user-fee policy, and to delay files that would help the outgoing party's remaining programmes. Advise the permanent secretary using the three classic principles.

steps.text: Permanence. Remaining in post is correct. The civil service is not emptied when the government changes; that is how the ministry continues to function.

Neutrality. Delaying files to spite the outgoing party, or to favour the new one beyond lawful instructions, would be partisan. The official must implement the new government's lawful policy and must not sabotage either side.

Anonymity. Appearing on television as the public defender of a controversial policy would break anonymity. The minister should make the political case; the permanent secretary should brief, draft and implement, not campaign.

Draw the line. If the minister issues a lawful instruction to prepare a user-fee circular, the official obeys. If the minister asks for a party rally speech in civil-service uniform, the official refuses.
State the accountability point. When the policy fails, the National Assembly summons the minister, not the anonymous official — which is why the official must not become the public face.

blocks.answer: Stay in post (permanence), implement lawful policy for whichever party is in power without sabotage (neutrality), and keep out of public defence of the policy (anonymity) — the minister, not the permanent secretary, is the political face

blocks.title: NEPA/PHCN and NITEL as corporation examples
blocks.text: When a question asks for examples of public corporations in Nigeria, NEPA (later PHCN) and NITEL are the safe historical pair. Add the Nigerian Railway Corporation if you need a third. Do not cite the Federal Inland Revenue Service or the police — those are services or departments, not commercial public corporations. And never write that a permanent secretary is elected.

points: The civil service is the permanent professional body that advises ministers and implements policy.
Its features include hierarchy, impartiality, merit recruitment, expertise, permanence, anonymity and neutrality.
Permanence means officials stay when governments change; anonymity means they are not the public face of policy; neutrality means they serve any ruling party without partisanship.
Ministers are political executives; permanent secretaries are administrative heads.
Public corporations are statutory bodies created to run utilities and strategic industries — historically NEPA/PHCN and NITEL in Nigeria.
Their problems (inefficiency, interference, corruption) led to privatisation and commercialisation from the late 1980s.
